momentum_away.summary: Outstanding run capped by a 4-2 win over Maccabi Tel Aviv on May 2; crushed Maccabi Haifa 3-0 in the reverse fixture in April.

simulation_phases.p1_0_15: Beitar press high with Atzili and Kalu stretching Haifa's back line. xG edge Beitar ~0.25 vs ~0.15. No goals likely; Haifa nervy.
simulation_phases.p2_15_45: Beitar dominate possession and create from set pieces — Carabali aerial threat. Most likely first goal: Beitar around 30-40'. xG Beitar ~0.7 vs Haifa ~0.4.
simulation_phases.p3_45_60: If Beitar lead, control mode; if level, Haifa push and home crowd lifts tempo. Bakhar likely brings on a forward.
simulation_phases.p4_60_75: Chasing Haifa leave gaps for Beitar's pace. Beitar's bench depth stronger.
simulation_phases.p5_75_90: Beitar keep probing — dropped points hand initiative to Be'er Sheva. Haifa's slump and lack of stakes blunts late urgency.

key_factors: Beitar in red-hot form, fighting for title
Beitar won reverse fixture 3-0 in April
Haifa miss CB Pedrao; defense leaking goals
Stakes asymmetry: Beitar must win, Haifa mid-table
narrative: Beitar Jerusalem arrive in Haifa on a five-match winning run with a one-point lead over Hapoel Be'er Sheva and the title in their hands. Maccabi Haifa are mid-table fifth, have leaked goals heavily over the last month, lost the April reverse 3-0, and miss CB Pedrao. The home crowd is capped near 5,000 due to wartime restrictions, blunting the usual Sammy Ofer advantage. Sim leans Beitar but with real downside variance.
